assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology from proglucagon processing and incretin action through to durable receptor agonists is a rare complete arc from basic endocrinology to a transformative therapy, with large effects on glycaemia, body weight and cardiometabolic outcomes. The discovery is clear, original and has strong, still-expanding impact.
assessment.attribution: Credit is spread over many contributors. Holst (incretin physiology, GLP-1 secretion and action), Drucker (GLP-1 biology and therapeutic translation) and Knudsen (design of long-acting acylated analogues behind liraglutide and semaglutide) form a coherent three-person configuration. Mojsov's contribution to identifying the active GLP-1 peptide is not included because of the three-laureate cap, and the allocation of that credit is unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many large randomized trials and real-world data, with a stable interpretation. Recognition is timely and arguably pressing given the therapeutic impact.
uncertainties: Contested priority for identifying the bioactive GLP-1 peptide, with Mojsov and others (e.g., Habener) possibly deserving credit; I cannot verify the details.
Long-term safety and the full mechanistic picture of weight loss are still being studied.
Dividing the prize between basic physiology and the industrial development of the drugs is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineering patients' T cells with chimeric antigen receptors produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies, a new therapeutic modality (living drugs) with approved products. Importance and impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain (early costimulated CAR design), June (clinical translation, CD19 CAR-T in CLL) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer, early gene-engineered TCR and CAR trials) are a plausible trio. Eshhar and others are not credited in the list, so the configuration may leave out an important originator.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and a decade of clinical follow-up confirm efficacy in hematologic cancers. Results in solid tumors are limited, and the toxicity profile (CRS, neurotoxicity, secondary T-cell malignancy signals) is still being characterized, but the core finding is mature.
uncertainties: Unlisted originators, such as the chimeric-receptor concept, may complicate a fair allocation.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancies, is still being assessed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Identification of TOR as the target of rapamycin and the demonstration that it controls cell growth in response to nutrients opened a whole field of growth control, with relevance to cancer, metabolism, ageing and immunosuppression. The discovery is original and conceptually unifying.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered the TOR genes and their role in growth control in yeast, and is the clear central figure. Schreiber's work on the FKBP12-rapamycin complex and mTOR as the target is a reasonable second contribution. Sabatini's mammalian mTOR work is important but I would not include him given the ambiguity of his record; I cannot verify the specifics here.
assessment.maturity: Very well confirmed across yeast, mammals and clinical use (rapalogs). The pathway's interpretation has become more complex (mTORC1/2) but the core finding is stable and recognition is not premature.
uncertainties: Exact allocation among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and the Heitman, Hall and Movva group is debatable.
Clinical impact of rapalogs is narrower than the basic-science impact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new form of organelle-to-nucleus signalling that controls the proteostasis capacity of the ER, with consequences for secretory cells, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. This is a mechanistically clear, fundamental discovery.
assessment.attribution: Mori (identification of the IRE1-HAC1/Hac1 transcription pathway in yeast and ATF6 in mammals) and Walter (IRE1 as kinase/RNase, unconventional splicing of HAC1 mRNA, later ISRIB work) are the decisive figures, and the two-person configuration is clean.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed over decades, conserved from yeast to mammals, with a stable mechanism. Recognition is timely, as the prize has not gone to this area, although the translational output (e.g. ISRIB, IRE1 inhibitors) is still early.
uncertainties: Other contributors (e.g., Ron, Harding, Kaufman, Shamu, Cox) may deserve credit and are not on the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience and physiology a general tool for causal, millisecond-precision control of defined cell types, and the microbial rhodopsins now permeate research from circuits to the heart and retina. Impact on method and discovery is very large, and the work is a clear invention.
assessment.attribution: Credit is very diffuse. Deisseroth and Boyden (neuronal channelrhodopsin expression), Nagel, Bamberg and Hegemann (channelrhodopsin characterisation) and Miesenböck (the first genetically targeted photostimulation of neurons) all have strong claims. A three-person limit forces hard choices, and I propose Miesenböck, Deisseroth and Hegemann as a compromise that covers the concept, application and molecular discovery.
assessment.maturity: Mature, widely reproduced, and used in thousands of labs. Clinical optogenetics (retinal vision restoration) is early but real.
uncertainties: Attribution is deeply contested and may be the main barrier.
The proposed trio omits Nagel, Bamberg and Boyden, who made decisive contributions.
The tool's contribution to medicine proper, as opposed to experimental science, is indirect.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense oligonucleotides that redirect SMN2 exon 7 splicing led to nusinersen, the first disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, which changed a fatal infantile disease. It links a mechanistic RNA-processing insight directly to a transformative treatment and established a platform for splice-switching drugs.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (identification of splicing regulatory elements in SMN2 and the antisense strategy) and Bennett (oligonucleotide chemistry and drug development at Ionis) are the central contributors. Other groups, such as Hua and Gurney, are not credited here, and the question of academic versus industrial credit is open.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy has been confirmed in multiple trials and in long-term real-world follow-up, and the approach has been extended to other genetic diseases. The platform is mature enough for recognition.
uncertainties: Attribution between academic and industrial contributors, and omitted collaborators, is not fully resolved.
Variable response in later-treated patients and the competing gene-therapy and small-molecule options complicate the narrative.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib validated a single oncogenic kinase as a therapeutic target in CML and turned a lethal leukemia into a chronic condition; the discovery established the paradigm of molecularly targeted therapy. Importance and clarity are very high.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (drug discovery and biochemistry at Ciba-Geigy), Druker (clinical development and preclinical demonstration of selectivity) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and second-generation inhibitors) form a natural trio, though the original BCR-ABL discovery (Rowley, Witte, Baltimore and others) lies outside the credited set.
assessment.maturity: More than two decades of survival data; the interpretation is stable, so the work is mature. A concern is that it may be considered already recognized via the Lasker award rather than a delayed candidate.
uncertainties: Upstream credit for the BCR-ABL translocation and kinase function is not in the candidate and might be seen as essential.
Industrial versus academic allocation is debatable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Virus-like particle HPV vaccines prevent persistent infection and cervical precancer, with population-level evidence of declines in cervical cancer, and represent a landmark in cancer prevention. The prize recognized HPV's role in cervical cancer in 2008, so this would be a natural complement.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller (L1 VLP self-assembly and immunogenicity) and Frazer (L1/L2 VLP work leading to the Gardasil/Cervarix technology) are commonly credited. Others, such as Zhou, Kirnbauer and Rose, made early VLP contributions and may be disputed, and there is a well-known patent and priority history.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in large randomized trials and by registry data from vaccinated cohorts showing substantial declines in cervical neoplasia and cancer. It is mature and recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: Priority among Frazer, Zhou, Lowy, Schiller, Kirnbauer and others is contested.
Whether the committee views this as a vaccine-engineering advance, rather than a basic discovery, is uncertain.
